panels.title: Refresh-token reuse detected (ALERT-WORTHY)
panels.description: WHAT: rate of refresh-token REUSE detections — a rotated/superseded refresh token replayed after it was already exchanged. HOW: rate() over the counter stacks_auth_refresh_reuse_detected_count_total, emitted by Stacks.Accounts.check_token_family/3 on the family-burn branch when the presented jti is neither the family's current token nor a within-grace predecessor. MEANS: this should sit flat at ZERO in healthy operation — the reuse gate only fires on a genuinely stale/forged token, and every hit burns the whole token family. WATCH: ANY non-zero value is alert-worthy — it means a refresh token was replayed (possible theft/replay attack); investigate the affected user, confirm the burned family, and treat a sustained rise as an active credential-compromise incident.

panels.title: Session absolute-cap expiries
panels.description: WHAT: rate of sessions force-expired by the absolute 7-day lifetime cap, tagged by reason (currently only lifetime_cap). HOW: rate() over stacks_auth_session_expired_count_total, emitted by AuthController.refresh/2 when a refresh is refused because the session has exceeded its window measured from ORIGINAL issue (the presented token is revoked and the client is bounced to /login). MEANS: a low, steady background rate is normal — it is simply users whose 7-day session finally aged out and who must re-authenticate. WATCH: a sharp spike means many sessions hit the cap at once (e.g. a cohort that all logged in ~7 days ago) and will produce a matching re-login / login surge; a change to the cap config will visibly shift this series.

panels.title: Login failures by type
panels.description: WHAT: rate of failed login attempts, split by type (invalid_credentials / email_unconfirmed / missing_params / account_locked / service_busy). HOW: rate() over stacks_auth_login_failure_count_total, emitted by AuthController.login/2 with a bounded whitelisted failure-type atom (never the submitted email/password). MEANS: a low invalid_credentials trickle is normal user error; the shape tells you WHY logins fail. WATCH: an invalid_credentials spike concentrated in time is a brute-force / credential-stuffing signal (cross-check the auth rate-limit 429s); a service_busy climb points to Argon2 pool saturation, and an email_unconfirmed climb points to a broken confirmation-email flow.

panels.title: Registrations by result
panels.description: WHAT: rate of user-registration attempts, split by result (ok / error). HOW: rate() over stacks_auth_registration_count_total, emitted by AuthController.register/2 with a bounded result atom. MEANS: the account-creation (right-to-account) throughput — a steady ok rate is healthy signup flow, and some error background is normal (duplicate email, weak password). WATCH: an error rate that dominates ok means registration is broken for real users (validation regression, DB fault) or is under abuse (bot signups probing taken emails); a sudden ok spike can indicate a signup campaign or automated account creation worth correlating with the login panels.

panels.title: JWT issued by context (login vs refresh)
panels.description: WHAT: rate of Guardian JWTs actually handed to a client, split by context (login = interactive sign-in issuance / refresh = silent-renewal rotation issuance). HOW: rate() over stacks_auth_jwt_issued_count_total, emitted once per minted token in AuthController.login/2 and refresh/2. MEANS: the refresh:login ratio is the health indicator — in steady state refresh should dominate (clients silently renew far more often than they log in fresh). WATCH: a collapse of the refresh series toward zero while login stays flat means the SPA's silent-renewal interceptor is failing and users are being pushed back to interactive login; a login spike without a matching prior refresh drop suggests mass re-authentication (correlate with the session-cap panel).

panels.title: Refresh-revoke failures
panels.description: WHAT: rate of failures to revoke the OLD token during a refresh rotation. HOW: rate() over stacks_auth_refresh_revoke_failed_count_total, emitted by AuthController.refresh/2 when Guardian.revoke of the presented token fails (the action still mints a fresh token, so rotation degrades rather than breaks). MEANS: this should be flat at ZERO — every rotation is expected to revoke its predecessor cleanly. WATCH: any sustained non-zero value means old refresh tokens are being left live past rotation (a weakened-rotation / lingering-credential security concern); investigate Guardian/guardian_tokens DB health, and treat it as adjacent to the reuse-detected panel since un-revoked old tokens widen the replay window.

panels.title: MFA verify (success vs failure)
panels.description: WHAT: rate of MFA verification attempts (TOTP codes and recovery codes), split by outcome (success / failure). HOW: rate() over stacks_auth_mfa_verify_count_total, emitted by Stacks.MFA.verify_totp/2 and verify_recovery_code/2 with a bounded outcome atom (never the code or secret). MEANS: mostly-success with an occasional failure is normal MFA friction (a mistyped or clock-skewed code). WATCH: a failure series that spikes or dominates success is either brute-forcing of a second factor (especially against admin/owner accounts) or a systemic problem such as TOTP clock drift; a total drop to zero after MFA is in use can mean the verification path is broken and legitimate users cannot complete sign-in.
